topic: Failing to Use Tag Dispatch for Overload Resolution
explanation: Assumption: The most direct way to resolve template ambiguity is to apply complex constraints (like SFINAE) directly to the function signature. Reality: When dealing with overloaded functions (especially templates), relying solely on signature complexity to guide resolution is fragile. A cleaner, more robust approach is Tag Dispatching. Why It Fails: Failing to use Tag Dispatching means that whenever a type needs to be excluded from a universal reference template (e.g., preventing the template from being chosen when a non-template overload exists), the developer must resort to verbose and error-prone SFINAE clauses. This anti-pattern obscures the function's intent and increases the risk of C6 (Overload Collision) because the constraint mechanism is difficult to manage. Tag Dispatch provides a clear path for the compiler to choose the most specialized (non-template) implementation first, relying on runtime polymorphism rather than complex template machinery for resolution.
practical_example: A logging system handles several types by value for simplicity, but needs to exclude user-defined types (UDTs) from an optimizing universal reference template. Without Tag Dispatching, the universal reference template aggressively consumes all UDT inputs, requiring maintenance of massive SFINAE clauses.
keywords: Tag Dispatching, SFINAE alternative, Template dispatch pattern, Overload resolution guidance
